title: Testing Architecture
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: DGX Evaluation for Textbook Generation
description: A step-through architecture diagram of a laptop, two home networks, the internet, Tailscale, and two DGX systems, showing which machine does each job when a local model generates textbook content.

learningObjectives: Explain which machine does each job in a local-model evaluation
Identify which data crosses each network boundary
Distinguish the Tailscale coordination server from the encrypted tunnel
Explain why a unified-memory GPU shares its memory with the CPU
prerequisites: What SSH is and what a home router does
The difference between a model and the program that runs it

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through worked example with concrete components visible at every step
keyQuestions: Which components could read a generation prompt?
Which components see only encrypted packets?
What does the coordination server learn about the machines?
What changed when the harness moved from the laptop to the DGX?
commonMisconceptions: The Tailscale coordination server carries the data. It carries only keys and addresses.
The GPU has its own memory. On this system it shares 128 GB of unified memory with the CPU.
The harness and the model are the same thing. The harness is the agent loop; the model generates the tokens.
assessmentOpportunities: Sketch the generation loop from memory and mark the boundary it never crosses
Name the machines that take part in each flow before reading the explanation
